table.role: Self-hosted agent runtime: polls Telegram, runs the active LLM agent, executes shell via TOOLS.md flows + exec approvals.
Linux environment hosting the gateway, agents, schedulers, and Ollama under Windows.
systemd --user supervises the gateway in WSL; NSSM runs Windows-side keepalive + Kaze services; Task Scheduler fires agent jobs.
Specialist agent logic — Yubin, Kakei, Asa, Koe, Sentry, bridges. urllib/sqlite3/imap, minimal third-party deps.
Orchestration shells for digests, briefings, health checks, and Task Scheduler entry points.
Lightweight static dashboard server (agents, tasks, roadmap, sentry status) on 127.0.0.1:18800.
Primary inference: gemma4:26b (agent default), gpt-oss-20b (main agent), qwen3:8b (Kaze fallback), qwen3-vl (vision/OCR).
Kaze digest primary provider — @cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct on the free tier, with automatic Ollama fallback.
gpt-5.4 available through an OAuth profile (rennesan@gmail.com) for select agent work.
RSS/Atom parsing for Kaze; combined with ThreadPoolExecutor fetch and SequenceMatcher de-dup.
Local on-device transcription of Telegram voice notes (small.en default). Nothing leaves the machine.
edge-tts Microsoft neural voices (online, default); Piper local offline fallback; dots.tts GPU clone (parked).
Yubin mailbox access (imap.gmail.com:993 / smtp.gmail.com:587) for maia.quiddam@gmail.com via app password.
Kakei ledger (bills + expenses tables) at ~/.openclaw/workspace-kakei/kakei.db. No central app DB.
Durable archive for Kaze/Yubin output; UI driven via Chrome session + qwen3-vl vision (no Google API).
Inbound/outbound messaging. Telegram polled by the gateway; LINE accounts for tasuke/naya/kaze.
Permanent named tunnel publishing the Kaze news page at kaze.quiddityinnovations.com.
repo/ holds the curated, non-secret agent scripts + config templates (secrets excluded by design).

descriptions.title: TOOLS.md is the architecture, not a config file
descriptions.body: The defining design choice of OpenClaw is that capabilities are declared in a Markdown file the LLM reads every turn. ~/.openclaw/workspace/TOOLS.md (1,262 lines) opens with GLOBAL_CONTEXT_RULES_v3 — a TALK/DO/PRIVATE permission firewall evaluated as ordered gates (first match wins) — then lists conversation flows: natural-language patterns mapped to shell commands. Wiring a new capability is 'add a section, restart the gateway' rather than writing a bot or a webhook. The version-controlled copy lives at repo/scripts/tasuke/TOOLS_ADDITIONS.md so it can be diffed and re-applied after an openclaw upgrade rewrites the live file.

descriptions.title: Local-first LLM with a free cloud edge
descriptions.body: Inference is primarily local via Ollama (gemma4:26b agent default, gpt-oss-20b main agent, qwen3-vl for vision/OCR), keeping data on-machine and cost near zero. Kaze's digests are the exception: they use Cloudflare Workers AI's free tier as primary with automatic Ollama fallback, routed through one place — kaze-llm-provider.py. That router also sets think=false for reasoning models so the response field is populated, and strips residual <think> tags. No script bypasses the router.

descriptions.title: Voice runs locally, speaks neurally
descriptions.body: Koe transcribes with whisper.cpp on-device (ffmpeg -> 16kHz mono WAV -> whisper), so voice notes never leave the machine. For output, koe-tts-router.py picks an engine: edge-tts (Microsoft Azure neural, free, online, default) detects each paragraph's language and uses a native female voice (pt-BR-FranciscaNeural, en-US-JennyNeural, es/ja/fr); Piper is the offline fallback; dots.tts is a GPU voice-cloning engine that is parked disabled because it reliably speaks only EN/ZH.

descriptions.title: Supervision spans two worlds
descriptions.body: OpenClaw straddles WSL and Windows. Inside WSL, systemd --user supervises the gateway (hot-reloading on config change) and a cron runs the Sentry health check + the 30-minute NotebookLM cookie copy. On the Windows side, NSSM runs OC-Keepalive-Service (rebuilds the WSL port proxy on boot, watches OAuth token expiry), QI_KazeConfigAPI, and QI_KazeNewsTunnel; Task Scheduler fires the agent jobs (Kaze x4, Yubin x2, Asa 7AM, Kakei Sunday, Sentry drift). keep-wsl-alive.ps1 keeps the distro warm.

descriptions.title: No central database — everything is files + small stores
descriptions.body: There is no application database. State lives in per-agent workspaces under ~/.openclaw/workspace-<agent>/, JSON config files (kaze-feeds.json, friendly-bots.json, shared-chats.json, bot-voices.json), and a single SQLite ledger for Kakei. Secrets live under ~/.openclaw/secrets/ (chmod 600), with templates committed to repo/ but never the real values. This keeps the system auditable, diffable, and cheap to back up.
